answer: Each agent must stake a bond tied to a unique verified identity, and voting power scales with stake locked over time. A sybil attacker creating many identities must fund each bond separately, multiplying capital at risk with no extra reward, so the attack becomes unprofitable. Like a single orchard requiring years of growth before harvest, trust accrues slowly, and every heartbeat pulse of the network verifies stake freshness, while a signed sonnet binding identity to bond prevents cheap duplication.
